stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and null spec — story needs full requirements elaboration for live preview across GO, UP, and MX platforms. openspec runs first to define AC and technical depth; speckit follows to harden testability, security, and edge-case coverage for multi-platform real-time preview complexity.

agentContributions.notes: Story adds Live Preview capability for Contentstack CMS. No existing implementation found. The useContent hook (236 callers) is the central attachment point — any Live Preview SDK must integrate there to propagate real-time updates to all consumers. Contentstack's Live Preview SDK typically requires initialization at the app/provider level and a listener within the content hook.

Openspec produced empty acceptanceCriteria, so all criteria are new. I built them from the story title, description, technical notes, and openspec's note about useContent being the central attachment point with 236 callers. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 establish the core real-time-no-refresh requirement; (2) AC-3 covers rapid sequential edits (debounce/throttle edge case); (3) AC-4/AC-5 tie to the specific files listed (ContentstackLink, contentCard); (4) AC-6 ensures cross-brand parity as the title demands GO, UP, MX; (5) AC-7 ensures zero-impact graceful degradation when preview is off; (6) AC-8/AC-9 cover connection interruption and recovery; (7) AC-10 covers invalid/expired token; (8) AC-11 covers multi-consumer propagation (critical given useContent's 236 callers); (9) AC-12 covers security of preview credentials; (10) AC-13 covers editor navigation reconnection; (11) AC-14 covers cache-miss on new content; (12) AC-15 covers malformed data resilience. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I did not have access to the actual file contents of useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, etc. If the current implementation has specific patterns (e.g., SSR vs CSR, Next.js ISR, custom caching layers), some ACs may need adjustment. In particular, the 'within 5 seconds' threshold in AC-1 is a reasonable default but should be validated against Contentstack SDK's actual event latency.
